items.description: Implements atomic preflight and commit semantics so an invalid batch or audit target cannot cause partial file mutation, while a valid batch commits in order.
items.pass_condition: All atomic cancellation, no-partial-mutation, commit-order, and audit-preflight checks pass. Atomic success (including duplicate inputs) is independently read back: Zone.Identifier absent; main bytes/identity/length/attributes/creation/write times and all other stream names/bytes preserved. Audit success must agree with this observed state.
items.failure_reason: The implementation mutates files before completing preflight, mishandles atomic commit order, or permits an invalid audit target to reach mutation.

items.description: Provides a non-mutating WhatIf preview that distinguishes a marked file from an already-clean file and does not create audit output.
items.pass_condition: Both WhatIf status and no-mutation checks pass.
items.failure_reason: Preview mode performs the removal, creates audit output, or reports the wrong state.

items.description: Removes exactly the Zone.Identifier stream, matches its name case-insensitively, and reports Removed for a marked regular file.
items.failure_reason: The source mark remains, the case variant is missed, or the status does not describe actual removal.

items.description: Preserves the same primary file object, its bytes and timestamps, and unrelated alternate data streams, including for protected files.
items.pass_condition: The target ADS is removed and all identity, content, timestamp, attribute, read-only, and unrelated-stream checks pass.
items.failure_reason: The primary file was replaced or changed, timestamps or attributes were lost, or an unrelated stream was modified.

items.description: Processes a batch independently and rejects missing, directory, wildcard, ADS, and reparse-point inputs without modifying rejected data.
items.pass_condition: All invalid-input and continuation checks pass.
items.failure_reason: A bad input aborts later work, wildcard semantics leak into the API, or a non-regular input is treated as a file.

items.description: Writes parseable ordered JSONL audit entries that agree with returned path and status values, while retaining idempotent result behavior.
items.pass_condition: Audit, repeatability, duplicate ordering, and result-contract checks pass. Atomic success (including duplicate inputs) is independently read back: Zone.Identifier absent; main bytes/identity/length/attributes/creation/write times and all other stream names/bytes preserved. Audit success must agree with this observed state.
items.failure_reason: Audit lines are missing or out of order, repeat calls are not state-aware, or result fields violate the contract.

items.description: Appends one ordered JSONL audit line per input, including Failed entries, without truncating earlier evidence.
items.pass_condition: Appended audit evidence keeps one ordered line per input for both successful and failed entries.
items.failure_reason: Audit output is truncated on a repeat call, drops Failed entries, or reorders them against the results.

items.description: Decides validity and audit-target conflicts from the real file identity and the whole parent chain, not from the leaf path string: a path reached through a reparse-point parent is rejected, and an AuditPath that is the same file object as an input (hard link, different spelling or case) fails before any deletion.
items.pass_condition: All four parent-chain and file-identity checks pass: the rejected junction input and the conflicting audit target keep every stream and byte, and a hard-link duplicate is reported by file identity without replacing the file object.
items.failure_reason: Only the leaf is reparse-checked, the audit target is compared as a path string, or hard links to the same file are treated as unrelated or as a failure.

items.description: The audit target is validated as writable before any deletion, and a junction-parent path invalidates a batch even when the same file object is also reachable by a valid hard link.
items.pass_condition: Both checks pass: an unwritable audit parent fails before deletion (source mark and bytes untouched, no audit file), and a hard-link plus junction-parent batch cancels atomically without changing the shared file.
items.failure_reason: Deletion happens before audit writability is known, or a junction-parent entry is accepted because the same file is reachable through a valid hard link.

items.description: Confirms the outcome of a failed atomic rollback per file and names the files whose target stream could not be restored instead of hiding them behind a batch-level message.
items.pass_condition: The batch fails as a whole, the file whose removal never succeeded keeps every stream and byte, and any file whose target stream was deleted but could not be written back is named in the reported error.
items.failure_reason: A rollback failure is swallowed, an unrestorable file is reported as restored or not identified at all, or the whole batch is not reported as Failed.

items.description: Accepts the extended-length spellings (\\?\ and \\?\UNC\) for input paths and for -AuditPath, echoes them verbatim, and reaches the same parent-chain, file-identity and audit-conflict decisions as the plain spelling.
items.pass_condition: A prefixed input is cleaned and echoed exactly as given with every other stream and byte preserved, a valid prefixed audit path is accepted and records the prefixed input, and a prefixed input still detects an audit target that is the same file object.
items.failure_reason: The prefix is treated as part of the file name, the colon of the drive specifier is mistaken for a stream separator, or a prefixed spelling weakens the identity and conflict checks.

items.description: Leaves every piece of metadata other than the target stream untouched: compression attribute, ACL and owner survive the clean and the file is never rebuilt.
items.pass_condition: A compressed file carrying an extra access-control entry is still cleaned, keeps its compressed attribute, identical ACL descriptor and owner, and keeps every unrelated stream byte-for-byte.
items.failure_reason: The compression attribute is lost, the ACL or owner changes, or the clean only works by rebuilding the file.

score_rule_note: No weights and no partial credit: the score is binary over the fixed required testcase set. Reward 1 only when every required F2P/P2P was really collected, executed and passed; any failure, skip, error or missing testcase is 0/INVALID. The per-item mapping below is reporting metadata only and does not weight the score.
